findings.issue: Tile-budget violations could produce a native file that would not reopen
findings.evidence: Merging two 200-tile layers produced a 400-tile layer, while the native decoder accepts at most 256. Merge and Duplicate now reject unsafe storage growth before mutation; live stamps update the global tile count as each tile is allocated.

findings.issue: Paste could overflow a native identifier and crash
findings.evidence: With next_id = u32::MAX, selectionPaste panicked on += 1. It now returns an error before recording a change.

findings.issue: Import decoded masks before enforcing its memory budget
findings.evidence: Previously every RLE mask was expanded before the final layer_bytes check; many empty layers with huge masks bypassed the per-pixel allocation check. Preflight now validates total decoded storage and RLE values before allocating planes; masks decode directly to bytes.

findings.issue: Moving a group left its off-canvas ink behind
findings.evidence: A mark at (-20,40), moved with its group by +40 px, stayed at its old position. The shared bounded remapper now moves interior, exterior and masks transactionally.

findings.issue: Flip Canvas did not reflect off-canvas pixels
findings.evidence: Horizontal flip of a 128-pixel canvas left x=-20 unchanged instead of moving it to x=147. Both axes now remap the complete layer.

findings.issue: A transform beyond exterior bounds could erase the artwork
findings.evidence: A +10000 px translation returned success and silently discarded every painted pixel. Transforms outside supported storage now fail with the original state intact.

findings.issue: Merge across a folder boundary lost group appearance
findings.evidence: Merging a blue layer inside a 25%-opacity group onto a root red layer discarded the folder opacity. Cross-folder merges now require moving layers to the same group first.

findings.issue: Paste duplicated source ink outside the selection
findings.evidence: The paste implementation cloned the source Layer including its entire exterior map. A rectangular interior copy therefore pasted unrelated exterior ink as well. The new layer now contains only clipboard pixels.

findings.issue: Group ID exhaustion could create duplicate folders
findings.evidence: saturating_add at the maximum group ID reused the ID, leaving a document that could not reload. Exhaustion is checked before mutation; maximum IDs are rejected on import.

findings.issue: A delayed Add Layer result could replace the new-group form
findings.evidence: A deterministic blocked-worker test clicked Add then Group. The late thumbnail callback replaced the name form. The Add path now captures the destination and panel revision at click time.

findings.issue: Unbounded empty-layer metadata could exhaust the UI and JNI
findings.evidence: Empty planes shared one buffer, so a small native file could contain thousands of layers without hitting the pixel budget. Both native and Vector decoders now validate a 4096-layer metadata ceiling before rendering; normal painting is still constrained by the existing memory budget.

findings.issue: Thin imported images became blank layers
findings.evidence: Importing a 1×2048 opaque image into 64×64 rounded the fitted width down to zero. Both fitted dimensions now retain at least one pixel.

findings.issue: Transform preview ignored nested folder opacity
findings.evidence: Two nested 50%-opacity folders should preview alpha≈64; the old preview rendered alpha=255. The preview now composites nested group scopes and applies exterior display opacity after compositing.

findings.issue: Renaming a personal brush removed it from Recent
findings.evidence: Recent stored names rather than stable IDs. Renaming a saved brush made its entry unresolvable. Entries now use custom IDs/builtin keys and migrate legacy names on read.

findings.issue: Explicit layer actions could affect the wrong active layer
findings.evidence: Duplicate/Delete accepted an index but operated on the active layer instead. A queued UI selection could therefore change the target. Native actions now honor the explicit index, and swipe actions send one atomic request.

findings.issue: Canvas Flip expanded every shared empty plane
findings.evidence: Flipping four blank layers replaced their shared empty buffer with four independent buffers; many large blank/duplicated layers could exceed memory budgets. Remapping now allocates interior pixels lazily and Flip caches identical geometry with a preparation budget.
